reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection treats supplied demand_score values and fallback ids as sufficient demand evidence. The package exposes only need text, record/source ids, demand_score, and source_weight; it does not show observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes supporting market demand. The all-true selection mask therefore preserves every candidate, including unsupported/recompute and review-ledger needs, instead of rejecting or flagging weak demand evidence.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, and outcomes support demand claims
generic keyword matches and unrelated candidates are not accepted as demand
missing or contradictory evidence remains visible

reviews.decision_reason: evidence_normalization whitelists the eight record ids and truncates to an index window, but it does not normalize or expose market-demand evidence quality. Because the incoming selected_df already contains only asserted scores and need strings, retaining all allowed ids carries forward unsupported demand claims without visible caveats.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: normalization preserves evidence needed to judge market demand
unsupported or weak candidates remain visible as unsupported
bounded intermediate values are inspectable enough to verify row retention

reviews.decision_reason: provenance_assembly ranks records by asserted demand_score and emits source_id/source_weight, but those source fields are opaque and contain no observed customer-demand evidence. This makes the downstream deterministic recommendation depend on unsupported rankings rather than substantiated market demand.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: provenance supports demand ranking with observed evidence rather than background labels
deterministic recommendation can be produced from the emitted ordering
